description_full: Permian Resources Corporation, an independent oil and natural gas company, focuses on the development of crude oil and associated liquids-rich natural gas reserves in the United States. The company's assets primarily focus on the Delaware Basin, a sub-basin of the Permian Basin. Its properties consist of acreage blocks in Reeves County in West Texas and Lea County in New Mexico. The company was formerly known as Centennial Resource Development, Inc. and changed its name to Permian Resources Corporation in September 2022. The company was incorporated in 2015 and is headquartered in Midland, Texas.

financial_summary: Permian Resources Corporation is a large-cap energy business with a $18.2B market cap on $5.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +33% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 12% against a 9% cost of capital, a 4-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $3.6B in free cash flow — roughly 71 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.86× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -14.9% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.3× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 5.2×.

Shareholder yield of 2.5% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 4.6% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 2.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
